title: Cemeteries and a 'Monastery' at the Y.M.C.A., Jerusalem
author: J. H. Iliffe
location_note: Sports ground west of the Y.M.C.A. building, Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name.
reading: full (pp. 70-80; text from the DjVu XML, the searchtext file was refused with HTTP 500); plate leaves carry captions only
notes: Clearance Sept.-Oct. 1932 after levelling for a sports ground. Greek tombstone of a bishop of the Georgians mentioning the 'Tower of David'. The excavator first called one installation a 'bath', then in an additional note (p. 80) a cistern like the one at Qalandia; both labels kept in the subtype. The cave tombs were cut 'probably by enlarging small caves already existing' (not coded separately).

features.subtype: ashlar family mausoleum with three lead sarcophagi, built inside a disused cistern
features.period: third century AD (by contents; coin of Julia Domna type)
features.quote: A group of ashlar masonry tombs, apparently a family mausoleum

features.subtype: two rock-cut cave tombs with five graves cut in the floor (lead and wooden coffins, slab covers)
features.period: early third century AD (excavator; section heading 'c. second to third century')
features.quote: Two cave tombs, situated immediately behind and west of the masonry tombs

features.subtype: over forty rock-cut cist graves in two rows, slab-covered, institutional ('monastery') cemetery
features.period: fifth to seventh century AD (Byzantine and Umayyad coins)
features.quote: A group of rock-cut graves of a poorer type

features.subtype: disused plastered cistern into which the mausoleum was built
features.period: earlier than the third-century mausoleum; not otherwise dated
features.quote: it was built in a disused cistern, whose plastered walls

features.subtype: plastered cistern with descending flight of steps; second installation called a 'bath' with foot niches and sump, re-identified as a cistern (p. 80)
features.period: fifth century AD (plaster over Byzantine sherds; building occupied from the fifth century)
features.quote: usual descending flight of steps and was plastered all over

features.subtype: clay drain-pipes from mosaic floors; channel cut through a wall from a runnel to the 'bath'
features.quote: draining to one corner (the south- west) through clay drain-pipes
